prompt: Rewrite using a gerund as subject
source: It is relaxing to read before bed.
correct: Reading before bed is relaxing.
explanation: Gerundio como sujeto: <verb-ing> reemplaza a <It is ... to + verb>.

prompt: Rewrite using <to + infinitive> after the adjective
source: Running a marathon is difficult.
correct: It is difficult to run a marathon.
explanation: <It is + adjective + to + infinitive> es una alternativa al gerundio como sujeto.

prompt: Change the verb pattern to gerund
source: I stopped and I bought some milk.
correct: I stopped to buy some milk.
hint: <Stop to + verb> = stop in order to do something
explanation: <Stop to + infinitive> significa pausar una actividad para hacer otra.

source: I locked the door. I remember it clearly.
correct: I remember locking the door.
explanation: <Remember + gerund> significa que recuerdas haber hecho algo en el pasado.

source: Don't forget: you need to call your mother.
correct: Remember to call your mother.
explanation: <Remember + to + infinitive> significa no olvidar hacer algo en el futuro.

source: She is good at languages. She speaks them well.
correct: She is good at speaking languages.
explanation: Después de preposiciones (at, in, of, about, for), usa siempre la forma en gerundio.

source: Try not to make the same mistake again.
correct: Avoid making the same mistake again.
explanation: <Avoid> siempre va seguido de un gerundio, nunca de un infinitivo.

source: "Why don't we go to the beach?" he said.
correct: He suggested going to the beach.
explanation: <Suggest> va seguido de un gerundio (no de un infinitivo) cuando no hay objeto indirecto.

source: You could take an aspirin. Maybe it will help your headache.
correct: Try taking an aspirin for your headache.
explanation: <Try + gerund> significa experimentar o probar algo como posible solución.

source: He made an effort to open the jar, but he couldn't.
correct: He tried to open the jar, but he couldn't.
explanation: <Try + to + infinitive> significa hacer un esfuerzo o intento por hacer algo.

source: I told her the truth. Now I'm sorry about it.
correct: I regret telling her the truth.
explanation: <Regret + gerund> expresa arrepentimiento por una acción pasada.

source: She went to the library because she wanted to study.
correct: She went to the library to study.
She went to the library in order to study.
explanation: Infinitivo de propósito: <to + verb> o <in order to + verb> expresa razón o propósito.

source: I can't wait to see you next week.
correct: I look forward to seeing you next week.
I'm looking forward to seeing you next week.
hint: <To> here is a preposition, not part of infinitive
explanation: <Look forward to> es un phrasal verb donde <to> es una preposición → va seguido de gerundio.

source: When I was a child, I played outside every day.
correct: I used to play outside every day.
explanation: <Used to + infinitive> describe hábitos o estados pasados que ya no existen.

source: Living alone is normal for me now.
correct: I am used to living alone.
I'm used to living alone.
hint: <Be used to> + gerund = be accustomed to
explanation: <Be used to + gerund> significa estar acostumbrado a algo.

source: At first the noise bothered me, but now it doesn't.
correct: I got used to the noise.
I've got used to the noise.
I got used to hearing the noise.
explanation: <Get used to + gerund/noun> significa acostumbrarse a algo con el tiempo.

source: Students can use calculators in the exam.
correct: The teacher allows students to use calculators in the exam.
Students are allowed to use calculators in the exam.
explanation: <Allow + object + to + infinitive> o la pasiva <be allowed to + infinitive>.

source: The teacher obliged us to rewrite the essay.
correct: The teacher made us rewrite the essay.
explanation: <Make> + objeto + infinitivo sin <to> expresa obligación forzada.

source: My parents allowed me to go to the concert.
correct: My parents let me go to the concert.
explanation: <Let> + objeto + infinitivo sin <to> expresa permiso.

source: "I didn't steal the money," he said.
correct: He denied stealing the money.
explanation: <Deny> va seguido de gerundio. Significa afirmar que algo no es cierto.

source: Would it bother you if I opened the window?
correct: Would you mind me opening the window?
Do you mind if I open the window?
explanation: <Mind> va seguido de gerundio. <Would you mind + gerund?> = petición cortés.

source: I laugh every time I see that video. I can't control it.
correct: I can't help laughing every time I see that video.
explanation: <Can't help + gerund> significa ser incapaz de dejar de hacer algo, no poder controlarlo.

source: You should see that film. It's very good.
correct: That film is worth seeing.
That film is worth watching.
explanation: <Be worth + gerund> significa que algo merece tiempo o esfuerzo.

source: She studied for three hours yesterday.
correct: She spent three hours studying yesterday.
explanation: <Spend + time + gerund> describe cómo se empleó el tiempo.

source: He continued talking despite the interruption.
correct: He went on talking despite the interruption.
explanation: <Go on + gerund> significa continuar con la misma actividad.
